lesson_scope: Geometric volume and surface-area models, one-variable reduction, related-rate chains, backward rate reasoning, and end-only unit conversion.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: calculating rate of change of circle area from radial rate.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of differentiating geometric area formulas and applying chain rule.

hints: Recall the area of a circle: $A = \pi r^2$.
Apply the chain rule: $\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \dfrac{dA}{dr} \cdot \dfrac{dr}{dt} = 10\pi \times 3 = 30\pi\text{ cm}^2\text{ s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Write the formula for the area of a circle and differentiate with respect to $r$:
$$A = \pi r^2 \implies \frac{dA}{dr} = 2\pi r$$

Evaluate the derivative at $r = 5\text{ cm}$:
$$\left.\frac{dA}{dr}\right|_{r=5} = 2\pi(5) = 10\pi$$

Apply the chain rule using $\dfrac{dr}{dt} = 3\text{ cm s}^{-1}$:
$$\frac{dA}{dt} = \frac{dA}{dr} \cdot \frac{dr}{dt} = 10\pi \times 3 = 30\pi\text{ cm}^2\text{ s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates $A = \pi r^2$ to obtain $\dfrac{dA}{dr} = 2\pi r$ and evaluates at $r = 5$ as $10\pi$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: calculating volume rate of change for an expanding cube.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of cube volume derivative and rate computation.

hints: Volume of a cube of side $x$: $V = x^3$.

walkthrough.text:
Write the volume formula for a cube and differentiate:
$$V = x^3 \implies \frac{dV}{dx} = 3x^2$$

Evaluate at side length $x = 10\text{ cm}$:
$$\left.\frac{dV}{dx}\right|_{x=10} = 3(10)^2 = 300\text{ cm}^2$$

Apply the chain rule using $\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 0.2\text{ cm min}^{-1}$:
$$\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{dV}{dx} \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} = 300 \times 0.2 = 60\text{ cm}^3\text{ min}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates $V = x^3$ to obtain $\dfrac{dV}{dx} = 3x^2$ and evaluates at $x = 10$ as $300$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: solving for dr/dt of a sphere given volume rate dV/dt.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of sphere volume formula derivative and reversing rate chain.

hints: Solve the rate relation: $36\pi = 36\pi \cdot \dfrac{dr}{dt} \implies \dfrac{dr}{dt} = 1\text{ cm s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the volume formula of a sphere $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$:
$$\frac{dV}{dr} = 4\pi r^2$$

Evaluate the derivative at $r = 3\text{ cm}$:
$$\left.\frac{dV}{dr}\right|_{r=3} = 4\pi(3)^2 = 36\pi$$

Solve for $\dfrac{dr}{dt}$ using $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 36\pi\text{ cm}^3\text{ s}^{-1}$:
$$\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{dV}{dr} \cdot \frac{dr}{dt} \implies 36\pi = 36\pi \cdot \frac{dr}{dt} \implies \frac{dr}{dt} = 1\text{ cm s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates $V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$ to obtain $\dfrac{dV}{dr} = 4\pi r^2$ and evaluates at $r = 3$ as $36\pi$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: cylinder with fixed height, finding dr/dt from dV/dt.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of fixed-height cylinder volume derivative.

hints: Volume of a cylinder of fixed height $h = 8$: $V = \pi r^2 h = 8\pi r^2$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the volume formula with fixed height $h = 8\text{ cm}$ and differentiate:
$$V = \pi r^2 (8) = 8\pi r^2 \implies \frac{dV}{dr} = 16\pi r$$

Evaluate the rate of change of volume with respect to radius at $r = 5\text{ cm}$:
$$\left.\frac{dV}{dr}\right|_{r=5} = 16\pi(5) = 80\pi$$

Apply the chain rule to determine $\dfrac{dr}{dt}$:
$$\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{dV}{dr} \cdot \frac{dr}{dt} \implies 40\pi = 80\pi \cdot \frac{dr}{dt} \implies \frac{dr}{dt} = \frac{40\pi}{80\pi} = \frac{1}{2}\text{ cm s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates $V = 8\pi r^2$ to obtain $\dfrac{dV}{dr} = 16\pi r$ and evaluates at $r = 5$ as $80\pi$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: calculating volume rate of change for a square-based pyramid.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of pyramid volume rate calculation.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the pyramid volume formula $V = 3x^2$:
$$\frac{dV}{dx} = 6x$$

Evaluate the derivative at $x = 6\text{ cm}$:
$$\left.\frac{dV}{dx}\right|_{x=6} = 6(6) = 36\text{ cm}^2$$

Apply the chain rule using $\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 0.5\text{ cm s}^{-1}$:
$$\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{dV}{dx} \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} = 36 \times 0.5 = 18\text{ cm}^3\text{ s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates $V = 3x^2$ to obtain $\dfrac{dV}{dx} = 6x$ and evaluates at $x = 6$ as $36$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: solving for dr/dt given surface area rate of a sphere.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of sphere surface area derivative and reversing rate chain.

hints: Differentiate $A = 4\pi r^2$ with respect to $r$: $\dfrac{dA}{dr} = 8\pi r$.
Solve the rate relation: $64\pi = 32\pi \cdot \dfrac{dr}{dt} \implies \dfrac{dr}{dt} = \dfrac{64\pi}{32\pi} = 2\text{ cm s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the surface area formula $A = 4\pi r^2$:
$$\frac{dA}{dr} = 8\pi r$$

Evaluate at radius $r = 4\text{ cm}$:
$$\left.\frac{dA}{dr}\right|_{r=4} = 8\pi(4) = 32\pi$$

Solve for $\dfrac{dr}{dt}$ using $\dfrac{dA}{dt} = 64\pi\text{ cm}^2\text{ s}^{-1}$:
$$\frac{dA}{dt} = \frac{dA}{dr} \cdot \frac{dr}{dt} \implies 64\pi = 32\pi \cdot \frac{dr}{dt} \implies \frac{dr}{dt} = \frac{64\pi}{32\pi} = 2\text{ cm s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates $A = 4\pi r^2$ to obtain $\dfrac{dA}{dr} = 8\pi r$ and evaluates at $r = 4$ as $32\pi$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Easy: the learner forms a fixed-height square-based volume model, differentiates a quadratic, and reverses one direct rate chain to find the changing base length.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The source supports using a derived geometric volume model in a related-rate chain. This original fixed-height channel has a square base, gives volume rate rather than a length rate, and asks for the base-side rate through a quadratic model.

hints: Write the volume formula for a prism with square base $x$ and fixed height $6$: $V = 6x^2$.
Differentiate $V$ with respect to $x$ to get $\dfrac{dV}{dx} = 12x$.

walkthrough.text:
Express the volume $V$ of the square-based prism of side $x$ and fixed height $6\text{ cm}$:
$$V = 6x^2$$

Differentiate $V$ with respect to $x$:
$$\frac{dV}{dx} = 12x$$

Evaluate the derivative at $x = 4\text{ cm}$:
$$\left.\frac{dV}{dx}\right|_{x=4} = 12(4) = 48\text{ cm}^2$$

Apply the chain rule with $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 48\text{ cm}^3\text{ min}^{-1}$:
$$\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{dV}{dx} \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} \implies 48 = 48 \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} \implies \frac{dx}{dt} = 1\text{ cm min}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates to obtain $\dfrac{dV}{dx}=12x$ and evaluates at $x=4$ as $48$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Easy: the supplied one-variable volume model only requires a bracketed power derivative, evaluation at a stated height, and a forward rate chain in consistent units.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The source models volume as a cubic in liquid depth before using a rate chain. This original model uses V = 1/2(h+1)^3 - 1/2 at h = 3 with dh/dt = 0.4.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the given volume model $V = \frac{1}{2}(h+1)^3 - \frac{1}{2}$ with respect to $h$:
$$\frac{dV}{dh} = \frac{3}{2}(h+1)^2 \times 1 = \frac{3}{2}(h+1)^2$$

Evaluate $\dfrac{dV}{dh}$ at height $h = 3\text{ m}$:
$$\left.\frac{dV}{dh}\right|_{h=3} = \frac{3}{2}(3+1)^2 = \frac{3}{2}(16) = 24\text{ m}^2$$

Apply the chain rule using $\dfrac{dh}{dt} = 0.4\text{ m min}^{-1}$:
$$\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{dV}{dh} \cdot \frac{dh}{dt} = 24 \times 0.4 = 9.6\text{ m}^3\text{ min}^{-1} \quad \left(\text{or } \frac{48}{5}\text{ m}^3\text{ min}^{-1}\right)$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: combines elimination of the height variable in a cylinder volume model with evaluating dr/dt and transferring to dh/dt through the linear constraint.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The source combines a geometric cylinder formula with a linear relation between dimensions to obtain a single-variable derivative. This original task uses h = 10 - r.

hints: Substitute $h = 10 - r$ into the cylinder volume $V = \pi r^2 h$: $V = \pi r^2(10 - r) = 10\pi r^2 - \pi r^3$.
Differentiate with respect to $r$: $\dfrac{dV}{dr} = 20\pi r - 3\pi r^2$.

walkthrough.text:
Express the volume of the cylinder in terms of $r$ alone using $h = 10 - r$:
$$V = \pi r^2 h = \pi r^2 (10 - r) = 10\pi r^2 - \pi r^3$$

Differentiate $V$ with respect to $r$:
$$\frac{dV}{dr} = 20\pi r - 3\pi r^2$$

Evaluate $\dfrac{dV}{dr}$ at $r = 4\text{ cm}$ and solve for $\dfrac{dr}{dt}$:
$$\left.\frac{dV}{dr}\right|_{r=4} = 20\pi(4) - 3\pi(16) = 80\pi - 48\pi = 32\pi$$
$$\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{dV}{dr} \cdot \frac{dr}{dt} \implies 16\pi = 32\pi \cdot \frac{dr}{dt} \implies \frac{dr}{dt} = \frac{16\pi}{32\pi} = \frac{1}{2}\text{ cm s}^{-1}$$

Relate the rate of change of height to the rate of change of radius:
$$h = 10 - r \implies \frac{dh}{dt} = -\frac{dr}{dt} = -\frac{1}{2}\text{ cm s}^{-1} \quad \left(\text{decreasing at } 0.5\text{ cm s}^{-1}\right)$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: two-part question using cone geometry with a fixed aspect ratio r = (1/4)h, leading to a cubic volume model and solving for the rate of height increase.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The source eliminates the radius in a cone volume formula using a fixed ratio. This original task uses r = 1/4 h.

hints: Recall the formula for the volume of a cone: $V = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$.

walkthrough.text:
Start with the standard formula for the volume of a cone:
$$V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$$

Substitute the radius ratio $r = \frac{1}{4}h$ into the volume formula:
$$V = \frac{1}{3}\pi \left(\frac{1}{4}h\right)^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi \left(\frac{1}{16}h^2\right) h$$

Simplify the numerical coefficient:
$$V = \frac{\pi}{48}h^3$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding the rate of increase of liquid height in a cone from volume inflow rate.

hints: Use the chain rule: $25\pi = \dfrac{9\pi}{4} \cdot \dfrac{dh}{dt} \implies \dfrac{dh}{dt} = \dfrac{25\pi \times 4}{9\pi} = \dfrac{100}{9}\text{ cm min}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the volume expression from part (a) with respect to $h$:
$$\frac{dV}{dh} = \frac{d}{dh}\left(\frac{\pi}{48}h^3\right) = \frac{3\pi}{48}h^2 = \frac{\pi}{16}h^2$$

Evaluate $\dfrac{dV}{dh}$ at height $h = 6\text{ cm}$:
$$\left.\frac{dV}{dh}\right|_{h=6} = \frac{\pi}{16}(6^2) = \frac{36\pi}{16} = \frac{9\pi}{4}\text{ cm}^2$$

Solve for $\dfrac{dh}{dt}$ using $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 25\pi\text{ cm}^3\text{ min}^{-1}$:
$$\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{dV}{dh} \cdot \frac{dh}{dt} \implies 25\pi = \frac{9\pi}{4} \cdot \frac{dh}{dt} \implies \frac{dh}{dt} = 25\pi \times \frac{4}{9\pi} = \frac{100}{9}\text{ cm min}^{-1} \quad \left(11\frac{1}{9}\right)$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: two-part question connecting surface area rate of a cylinder to volume rate via the intermediary rate dr/dt.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Forming total surface area of a closed cylinder with fixed height. This original cylinder has h = 10.

hints: A closed cylinder has 2 circular ends of area $\pi r^2$ each, and curved surface area $2\pi r h$.
With height $h = 10$, total surface area $S = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r(10) = 2\pi r^2 + 20\pi r$.

walkthrough.text:
Sum the areas of the two circular bases and the curved surface area:
$$S = 2(\pi r^2) + 2\pi r h$$

Substitute the fixed height $h = 10\text{ cm}$:
$$S = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r(10) = 2\pi r^2 + 20\pi r$$

ai_rubric.observable: Includes the two circular ends to form $S=2\pi r^2+2\pi r(10)$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Linking surface area rate to volume rate via the radius rate in a cylinder.

hints: Differentiate $S = 2\pi r^2 + 20\pi r$ to get $\dfrac{dS}{dr} = 4\pi r + 20\pi$.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the surface area formula $S = 2\pi r^2 + 20\pi r$ with respect to $r$:
$$\frac{dS}{dr} = 4\pi r + 20\pi$$

Evaluate at $r = 2\text{ cm}$ and solve for $\dfrac{dr}{dt}$ using $\dfrac{dS}{dt} = 48\pi\text{ cm}^2\text{ s}^{-1}$:
$$\left.\frac{dS}{dr}\right|_{r=2} = 4\pi(2) + 20\pi = 28\pi$$
$$\frac{dS}{dt} = \frac{dS}{dr} \cdot \frac{dr}{dt} \implies 48\pi = 28\pi \cdot \frac{dr}{dt} \implies \frac{dr}{dt} = \frac{48\pi}{28\pi} = \frac{12}{7}\text{ cm s}^{-1}$$

Differentiate the volume $V = \pi r^2 (10) = 10\pi r^2$ with respect to $r$:
$$\frac{dV}{dr} = 20\pi r \implies \left.\frac{dV}{dr}\right|_{r=2} = 20\pi(2) = 40\pi$$

Calculate the rate of increase of the volume:
$$\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{dV}{dr} \cdot \frac{dr}{dt} = 40\pi \times \frac{12}{7} = \frac{480\pi}{7}\text{ cm}^3\text{ s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates $S$ to obtain $\dfrac{dS}{dr}=4\pi r+20\pi$ and evaluates at $r=2$ as $28\pi$.
Differentiates $V=10\pi r^2$ and finds $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=40\pi\left(\dfrac{12}{7}\right)=\dfrac{480\pi}{7}\text{ cm}^3\text{ s}^{-1}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: 3-part structured question on a rectangular prism with polynomial dimensions, requiring expanding S and V, inverting dS/dt to dx/dt, and calculating dV/dt.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Algebraic expansion of surface area and volume of a cuboid with linear algebraic dimensions x, x+2, x+5.

hints: Surface area of a cuboid: $S = 2(lw + wh + lh) = 2(x(x+2) + (x+2)(x+5) + x(x+5))$.
Expand and collect like terms: $x^2+2x + x^2+7x+10 + x^2+5x = 3x^2+14x+10 \implies S = 6x^2+28x+20$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate total surface area $S$ by summing the 6 rectangular faces:
$$S = 2\left[x(x+2) + (x+2)(x+5) + x(x+5)\right]$$

Expand the inside expressions and simplify:
$$x(x+2) = x^2+2x, \quad (x+2)(x+5) = x^2+7x+10, \quad x(x+5) = x^2+5x$$
$$\text{Sum} = 3x^2+14x+10 \implies S = 2(3x^2+14x+10) = 6x^2+28x+20$$

Expand the volume expression $V = l \cdot w \cdot h$:
$$V = x(x+2)(x+5) = x(x^2+7x+10) = x^3+7x^2+10x$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding dx/dt from surface area rate dS/dt.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate $S = 6x^2+28x+20$ with respect to $x$:
$$\frac{dS}{dx} = 12x + 28$$

Evaluate at $x = 3\text{ cm}$ and solve for $\dfrac{dx}{dt}$ using $\dfrac{dS}{dt} = 32\text{ cm}^2\text{ s}^{-1}$:
$$\left.\frac{dS}{dx}\right|_{x=3} = 12(3) + 28 = 36 + 28 = 64$$
$$\frac{dS}{dt} = \frac{dS}{dx} \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} \implies 32 = 64 \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} \implies \frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{32}{64} = \frac{1}{2}\text{ cm s}^{-1}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding dV/dt from dx/dt and derivative of V.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the volume expression $V = x^3+7x^2+10x$:
$$\frac{dV}{dx} = 3x^2 + 14x + 10$$

Evaluate $\dfrac{dV}{dx}$ at $x = 3\text{ cm}$:
$$\left.\frac{dV}{dx}\right|_{x=3} = 3(3^2) + 14(3) + 10 = 27 + 42 + 10 = 79\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate $\dfrac{dV}{dt}$ using $\dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{2}\text{ cm s}^{-1}$:
$$\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{dV}{dx} \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} = 79 \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{79}{2}\text{ cm}^3\text{ s}^{-1} \quad (39.5)$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: two-part question on a cone with h = 3r, requiring volume model in r, multi-step chain rule, and multi-unit conversions (m/min to cm/s).

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Substituting h = 3r into the volume of a cone V = 1/3 pi r^2 h.

hints: Volume of a cone: $V = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $h = 3r$ into the conical volume formula:
$$V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 (3r)$$

Simplify the expression:
$$V = \pi r^3$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding dh/dt in cm/s from inflow rate in m^3/min.

hints: Convert units: $\dfrac{8}{5\pi}\text{ m min}^{-1} \times \dfrac{100\text{ cm}}{1\text{ m}} \times \dfrac{1\text{ min}}{60\text{ s}} = \dfrac{8}{5\pi} \times \dfrac{5}{3} = \dfrac{8}{3\pi}\text{ cm s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the volume formula $V = \pi r^3$ with respect to $r$:
$$\frac{dV}{dr} = 3\pi r^2$$

Evaluate at $r = 0.3\text{ m}$ and solve for $\dfrac{dr}{dt}$ using $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 0.144\text{ m}^3\text{ min}^{-1}$:
$$\left.\frac{dV}{dr}\right|_{r=0.3} = 3\pi(0.3)^2 = 0.27\pi\text{ m}^2$$
$$\frac{dr}{dt} = \frac{dV/dt}{dV/dr} = \frac{0.144}{0.27\pi} = \frac{144}{270\pi} = \frac{8}{15\pi}\text{ m min}^{-1}$$

Relate the rate of height increase to the radius rate using $h = 3r$:
$$\frac{dh}{dt} = 3\frac{dr}{dt} = 3\left(\frac{8}{15\pi}\right) = \frac{8}{5\pi}\text{ m min}^{-1}$$

Convert $\dfrac{dh}{dt}$ from $\text{m min}^{-1}$ to $\text{cm s}^{-1}$:
$$\frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{8}{5\pi} \times \frac{100\text{ cm}}{60\text{ s}} = \frac{8}{5\pi} \times \frac{5}{3} = \frac{8}{3\pi}\text{ cm s}^{-1} \quad (\approx 0.849\text{ cm s}^{-1})$$

ai_rubric.observable: Uses chain rule to find $\dfrac{dr}{dt}=\dfrac{0.144}{0.27\pi}=\dfrac{8}{15\pi}\text{ m min}^{-1}$.
Converts to $\text{cm s}^{-1}$ by multiplying by $\dfrac{5}{3}$ to obtain $\dfrac{8}{3\pi}\text{ cm s}^{-1}$.
